verdicts.reason: A keeps the original reading order (quote mark, quote, attribution, then can) with no collisions, but the quote is shrunk from hero size to body-copy size, the can floats unanchored above the circle, and the bottom third is an empty circle. B puts the can first, which reverses the hierarchy, and pushes the quote and attribution onto the edge of the backdrop circle, an unintended overlap. B's quote is just as small, and its top half is product plus dead space.

A has no collisions and the quote leads, though the quote text is undersized and the circle at the bottom is empty decoration with dead space around the can. In B the quote is smaller still ('a little / bitter' wraps awkwardly), the quote and attribution sit across the circle's edge, and the can, placed first, competes with the quote as the focal point.

A has the smallest quote text of the set, with an orphaned 'gone too soon.' line. Its text block sits over the circle's edge, and it leads with the can, so the testimonial reads as secondary. B keeps the quote-first order with clean separation, but its quote is still far too small relative to the original hero and the lower half is mostly an empty circle.

A jams the quote mark near the top edge, sets the quote text tiny with a weak wrap ('and / gone too soon'), leaves a big gap before the can, and drops the logo onto the circle at the bottom edge, where it collides and loses emphasis. B has a cleaner structure: the logo is centred at the top and the quote, attribution and can follow in sequence with no collisions. B's flaws are an undersized quote and a dead circle at the bottom.
